_about: Public-domain Moses D. Hoge (Moses Drury Hoge, 1818-1899, Second Presbyterian Church, Richmond) for the Word Hoard: The Perfection of Beauty and Other Sermons (posthumous, 1904) and four sermons and addresses (1855-1875), raw Internet Archive OCR. A small shelf: most of what survives is by others about him. Not his grandfather Moses Hoge (1752-1820). Added 2026-10-10 by lane A, round 19 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted.

hoge-honorable-old-age: Honorable Old Age: A Sermon at the Funeral of Capt. Benjamin Sheppard (Richmond: H. K. Ellyson, 1855)
hoge-christian-statesman: The Christian Statesman: A Discourse at the Funeral of John Hemphill (Richmond: Enquirer Book and Job Office, 1862)
hoge-mission-field-south: Mission Field of the South, an address to the Evangelical Alliance (Richmond: Whig Job Office, 1873)
hoge-jackson-statue: Inauguration of the Jackson Statue: Introductory Address of Governor Kemper, and Oration of Moses D. Hoge (Richmond: R. F. Walker, 1875; a civic oration, shared with Kemper)
hoge-perfection-of-beauty: The Perfection of Beauty and Other Sermons (Richmond: Presbyterian Committee of Publication, 1904; posthumous)

_alternates.hoge-biographies: Moses Drury Hoge: Life and Letters, by Peyton Harrison Hoge (copyright 1899; IA mosesdruryhogeli00hoge); Life and Labors of Moses D. Hoge (anonymous, 1899); the 1899 memorial service; the 1890 forty-fifth anniversary commemoration
_alternates.hoge-perfection-copy: The Perfection of Beauty, second copy (IA perfectionofbea00hoge)
_alternates.moses-hoge-grandfather: His grandfather Moses Hoge (1752-1820): Sermons Selected from the Manuscripts (1821; IA sermonsselectedf00hoge) and Strictures upon a Pamphlet by Jeremiah Walker (1793): a different author, not shelved here

_excluded.hoge-contributions: Proceedings in Memoriam of Moncure and Ould (1883) and the Cooke Stonewall Jackson biography: contributions only
_excluded.hoge-brother: The Victory Won, a memorial of his brother W. J. Hoge, by T. V. Moore
